newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Power already private ahead of listing.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Power already private ahead of listing.

text.p: Singapore Power's chief Ho Kwon Ping said on Wednesday the state-owned company was already operating like a private company but whether it would be listed was up to the government.

"As far as we are concerned, the government is treating us as if we are like a privatised entity because the minute we are corporatised, we are not under the goverment any more, we are under Temesek Holdings," he said in an interview with Reuters.
Temesek Holdings is a state investment company and Singapore Power, which is due to lose its monopoly on power production in two years, was corporatised in 1995.

Asked about the company plans for listing, Ho said "We are operating as a private entity, so (the listing) does not really affect us, but it is really a question you should ask the minister," he added.
"The decision for the public listing of Singapore Power will be made by the goverment," Ho said.

The Singapore government has said it plans to list Singapore Power and to open up the power industry to the private sector in about two years. It plans to raise electricity tariffs by 12-14 percent before then.
Singapore Power was scheduled to be list in mid-1996, but the government delayed the move indefinitely.

Singapore's Public Untilities Board has said it was setting up a pool system in which independent power producers, transmission companies and other operators could bid to buy and sell power in a free market.
The board is studying regularity systems in countries like New Zealand, where a company has been set up to oversee the bidding process.
Ho told Reuters that in such a free market, there would be scope and possibily that Singapore would have a electricity exchange.
